title: Dawn codon — GPU lane quickrun
content:
Morning quickrun (short + noisy)

Context: personal scratchpad for today. Goal: get the small fleet warm, finish the 4-node rack swap, and confirm burst lane for evening canary. Keep notes messy.

Top priorities (ordered)
1) Warmup new p4d-24 nodes (rack A3) — confirm NVLink, driver 535 OK. (ETA 45m)
   - commands: ssh node-a3-0; sudo systemctl start nvidia-dcgm-exporter; sudo modprobe nvidia_uvm || true
   - quick checks: nvidia-smi topo -m; dcgmi discovery -l; journalctl -u nvidia-dcgm-exporter -n 200
   - expected: all 8 GPUs show MIG profiles enabled for tenant pools; if not, re-run /opt/gpu-tools/mig-init.sh

2) Preemptive drain for maintenance on rack B1 (midday window 13:00-14:00)
   - schedule: set drain tag on queue: curl -X POST ${SCHEDULER_API}/jobs/drain -d '{"rack":"B1","reason":"maintenance"}'
   - note: inform #infra-gpu-ops and add a heartbeat to handoff notes

3) Nightly burst-lane smoke (deploy config)
   - file: /repos/infra-configs/burst-lane.yaml (pull latest: git fetch && git checkout feature/burst-lane-telemetry)
   - sanity: run k8s job small-smoke-run to ensure batching logic works (qsize=32, max_latency=120ms)

Observability checks (quick)
- console: per-route latency (last 6h) -> expect 95p <= 140ms for short-gen model
- token cost: spike? look at token-meter per-customer for top 5 users
- DCGM: GPU temp median 65C, memory utilization baseline 12-20% idle
- Alerts to scan: GPU-power-surge, rack-network-loss, qsub-fail-rate > 3%

Snippets/cheatsheet I keep forgetting
- reclaim stale MIG groups: /opt/gpu-tools/mig-repair --dry-run then --apply
- quick nvlink map: nvidia-smi topo -m | grep NVLINK
- restart buddy service: sudo systemctl restart gpu-buddy || echo "buddy restart failed" && journalctl -u gpu-buddy -n 80

Decisions / open questions
- Should we lower default batcher max_tokens for burst-lane trials? pros: lower tail latency; cons: more token overhead per request. Tentative: set to 512 for smoke only.
- Can we route non-critical low-cost traffic to g4dn spare pool instead of p4d for the 2-hour evening slot? Need cost estimate from Pete (finance).

Handoff bullets for evening on-call
- Rack A3: left in ready state, nvlink validated, MIG groups sticky=true.
- B1: drain scheduled 13:00 — undo after maintenance with /scripts/undrain-rack B1 (owner: Ishaan).
- Canary: keep burst-lane flag ON until 22:00 unless errors > 5% or p95 latency > 300ms.

Mini retros from yesterday (notes)
- Cause of short-gen tail: batching queue starvation around 19:04 due to large embedding jobs. Mitigation: added a soft cap on embedding-worker tokens. Need to bake into optimize recommendations.
- Lesson: always run small-smoke-run locally before pushing burst yaml. Saved one rollback.

Temp TODOs (quick, actionable)
- [ ] ping Pete for g4dn cost delta (slack) — 10m
- [ ] add small-smoke-run to preflight CI for burst-lane PRs — 25m
- [ ] follow up on INFRA-1123 (NVSwitch flapping) — assign to SRE rotation
- [ ] dump last 24h dcgm metrics to /tmp/rowan-dcgm-<date>.tgz and upload to confluence page

Notes-to-self (random)
- If a node reports CUDA driver mismatch, check /etc/modprobe.d/ for leftover blacklist files.
- Keep a copy of the single-line warmup: ssh $NODE 'sudo systemctl start nvidia-dcgm-exporter && sleep 15 && dcgmi discovery -l'

End of quickrun — keep this file messy. Will tidy into confluence if we need to share.

-- rowan
